inline_comments.comment: This file carries a `> **Warning** ## THIS IS AN AUTOGENERATED FILE. DO NOT EDIT.` header at its top. All documentation edits must be made exclusively in the source tree at `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md`; the `docs/` directory is regenerated by the build pipeline and any changes made here directly will be overwritten and lost on the next docs build. Revert these changes from `docs/` — only the source-side edit is needed.

The generated file adds 5 sub-items (Octave Repo Index, News, Source Code, Function Reference, Bug Tracker), while the source file at `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` adds only 1 sub-item (`octave_mermaid_js`). The two files are immediately inconsistent. When the docs pipeline regenerates `docs/` from the source, the 4 extra sub-items in the generated file would be lost. The intended content must be decided in the source file and only reflected here via the pipeline.

The semver level is marked `major`, but `major` is reserved for breaking changes only. Adding a community integration listing to a documentation page is a new/additive feature at most, which maps to `minor`. Please change `major` to `minor`. Additionally, this changeset is identical to `.changeset/true-parrots-build.md` — one of the two duplicates should be deleted entirely.
This changeset is a duplicate of `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md` — both have identical content. Only one changeset file is needed per PR. Delete this file.

The semver level `patch` is for bug fixes. Adding a community integration documentation entry is an additive (new feature) change, which maps to `minor`. Change `patch` to `minor`. Note also that the other two changesets in this PR use `major`, so there are three conflicting semver signals across three changesets — only one changeset should exist, with the correct level.
Typo: "marmaid.js" should be "mermaid.js". The same typo appears in all three changeset files.

The top-level entry links to `https://octave.org/`, which is the GNU Octave product homepage rather than the integration-specific Mermaid documentation page. Per project conventions (see the Obsidian and Observable entries in the same list, which link directly to the platform's Mermaid-specific docs), the top-level link should point to the integration's own documentation page (e.g., `https://cnoctave.github.io/octave_mermaid_js/index.html` or the repo). Since GNU Octave itself doesn't natively support Mermaid, linking to the GNU Octave homepage is misleading — the sub-item link to the `octave_mermaid_js` repo is the real integration entry.

general_comments.comment: There are three changeset files in this PR (`.changeset/7123.md`, `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md`, `.changeset/true-parrots-build.md`) when only one should exist. Two are identical duplicates, and all three disagree on the semver level (`patch` vs. `major`). Remove the two duplicate files and reconcile on a single level. For a pure documentation addition to the community integrations list, `minor` is the most appropriate level (new/additive), though an argument can be made that a doc-only integrations listing does not require a changeset at all since it does not change any package's public API.

The changeset message text repeats the typo "marmaid.js" (should be "mermaid.js") and uses the vague phrasing "add doc to use marmaid.js in GNU Octave." Per project conventions, changeset messages should be phrased from the perspective of observable public API or user-visible behavior, naming the affected component concisely — for example: `feat: add octave_mermaid_js community integration to ecosystem docs`.
